real_defects.issue: 90-day tie counted at exactly 90 days (ctx.prev1 >= 90); Finance Act 2013 Sch 45 para 37 says more than 90 days. A leaver or arriver with exactly 90 days in an earlier year got a phantom tie, which can flip the verdict to resident (e.g. an arriver at 60 days with family, accommodation and work ties). An existing test (prev1: 90 -> resident) encoded the wrong rule; the ties-table page said "90 or more".

Country tie needed strictly more UK days than any other country (days > mostElsewhere); Sch 45 para 38(2) gives the tie when the UK draws for the greatest number of midnights. A leaver at a draw lost a tie and could be told not resident. An existing test asserted the wrong rule; the page and ties-table copy said "more ... than".
